item.content:encoded:
Couple places where this article confused me.

After bringing multiple subjects under their control, the SCP-570-1 instances and subjects

Is it possible to have multiple instances of 570-1 at the same time? That was never mentioned.

Subjects who were under SCP-570’s control will suffer no immediate side effects after being released, with the exception of a strong sense of longing

I assume this refers to the puppets, not the puppeteers? Might this be more clear if, throughout the article, the puppets were referred to as 570-2 or some such?

This effect is not universal, and will only manifest in subjects who previously displayed symptoms of depression and anxiety.

Seems bad form to describe an effect of the object that only affects a segment of the population (a) without making it clear at the beginning of the paragraph that that is the case and (b) without describing how everybody else is affected. I mean, presumably they're just skeeved out to have been made into a puppet. But if this thing has an effect on the emotions of the puppets that seems like an iffy assumption for the reader to make.

More generally, the article never explicitly says that the gloves compel the puppeteer to put on shows (unless they were formerly a puppet themselves?). If there's a persona behind the gloves that controls you once you put them on, or a compulsion to put on puppet shows, I'd like that to be more explicit. And either way, surely the identity of the puppeteer in the testing logs is worth mentioning - I couldn't tell if it was the original proprietor of the puppet shop putting on those shows.

Apologies if my comments are unclear - I'm not much of a writer so it stands to reason that I'm not the best editor. But overall this article felt like it could be greatly improved if a better editor than I gave it a thorough going-over.

Both this article and SCP-2991 make use of anomalous clothing. Wouldn't it be interesting if the fiber composition of these anomalies matched, as that would imply that such a composition is potentially anomalous in and of itself, and can be used to both create sapience in cloth in some cases, or override the sapience of other beings in others. As such, I am proposing the following addendum:

Addendum 2: Notes on SCP-570 Fiber Composition

Samples taken from the cotton fibers used by SCP-570 to link SCP-570-1 and its affected subjects have been shown to match the composition of initial samples taken from SCP-2991. Due to the possibility that this particular fiber composition maybe partially responsible for the effects of both anomalies, anomalous materials analysis on samples from both objects is currently underway.

If anyone has other/better examples that could be used here please leave a comment saying so!

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
"These strings are capable of controlling multiple victims, with the high-end of recorded “puppets” reaching up to 100 simultaneous connections. Despite this, only one action can be performed by the mass at once, as SCP-570 is incapable of issuing individual instructions. "

Then it's practically useless. You can't effectively control a group of people (up to 100) when you can issue only one order at the time, without any differentiation, by means similar to a puppeteer's strings. Since this uses a neural connection, and not a supernatural one, and not mental signals… You give them an order to "walk", but 47 of them face other direction, 18 of them falls down the cliff, 20 bump off the wall etc. You can either have a superior imperative (like obeying an order "charge"), when the target is behaving autonomously in large part, or a total micromanagement, when you control each unit directly. These gloves would be too cumbersome to use in my opinion.

An innovative idea, to be sure, but I have a problem with it.

I'd like everyone to read, rate, and comment on this article. I believe it could use additional attention.

I don't think this conserves weirdness effectively. And it lacks focus — it seems more effort was put into making it "balanced" than into making it interesting to read. And the tone is non-clinical in a few cases.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I really like this idea. I was expecting it to be a "thing what lets you control people" but I expected the control to be with the users mind. I like that it comes at great cost and that the strings themselves are breakable, it all seems like a great idea. Then the author starts throwing in things seemingly at random just to add to the mystery or whatever. You use your own muscle, for that matter why 93%? And what's that other 7%?. Then you also stop eating. Victims are incited towards becoming users by some inexplicably psychic force. Tendons get turned into super effective fiber optic cables I suppose but the actual field use of this bothers me, radio communication is effectively instantaneous and it doesn't require a hard connection so I'm confused as to what downside to radio/satellite communication is being overcome here at a 57% imrovement but there's also the decreased utility due to the hardware necessity.

All in all I love the idea but I think the author ran away with the need to make it unique…
